title: Principles of Cell Signaling: Signals, Receptors and Responses
method: Actual saved p.teaching-prose lexical count excludes headings, tables, figures, questions, answers, revision, references and UI. Whitespace cross-check 14015. Total article text includes supplemental content and expanded answers, excludes SVG and buttons; 155 distinct paragraphs, maximum pre-review pairwise word-set Jaccard 0.264.

comparator.comparison: Adjacent verified chapter recounted directly; 4.A.01 has comparable narrative depth, distinct foundational scope, separate practice and explicit mathematical assumptions.

scope_review: Revised merged CSIR–DBT Unit 4.A printed page 5, separate NET Unit 4.B printed page 3, archived MP SET Unit 4.B page 3 visually inspected. Academy roadmap covers cue types, receptor specificity, affinity, saturability, occupancy, dose–response, reception/transduction/effector/output, amplification, duration, brief delivery modes. Detailed receptor classification, individual mechanisms, feedback networks and cellular communication retained in subsequent nodes. Binding and time-course calculations are simplified one-step models, not specialist pharmacology.

coverage_360.foundations: Sections 1–4: purpose, physical/chemical inputs, information vs material, recognition
coverage_360.history: Section 9: cAMP identification and G protein coupling, controls and reconstitution
coverage_360.structure: Sections 2–3 and figures 2–3: receptor and ligand properties, membrane coupling
coverage_360.mechanism: Sections 4,9–11: relay, messenger, effector, catalytic gain
coverage_360.chemistry: Sections 3,5,10: noncovalent binding, thermodynamics, phosphorylation vs nucleotide binding
coverage_360.mathematics: Sections 5–8,11–12: occupancy, mass balance, rates, competition, response, gain and duration
coverage_360.evidence: Sections 7,9,14: binding assays, fractionation, rescue and causal controls
coverage_360.comparative: Sections 1–2,13: bacterial, plant and animal sensing and tissue differences
coverage_360.perturbation: Sections 3,7,14: competition, coupling loss, downstream bypass
coverage_360.exceptions: Sections 3,5–8,12: basal activity, depletion, kinetics, EC50 differences, sustained response
coverage_360.cross_concept: Membrane organization, enzymes and free energy, gene regulation and cell state
coverage_360.exam_reasoning: 52 original explained items including 24 Part C, eight worked problems and graph reasoning

review_pass_1: Internal scientific review verified reversible equilibrium assumptions, mass conservation, units, physical roots, thermodynamics, rate constants, response normalization, competition, receptor reserve model, phosphorylation chemistry, finite pool gain, steady state vs equilibrium, messenger dynamics, evidence limitations and pathway causality. Clarified cAMP historical inference and ligand-independent basal activity.
review_pass_2: Separate saved-source teaching/examination review against 4.A.02; revised 14 conceptual distractor sets with aligned explanations, referenced graph principles, added section-level source anchors, improved formula notation, checked all 52 answer keys and original SVG labels/attributes and targets. Source reading reviewed; no external examiner calibration.

arithmetic_checks.method: Independent JavaScript recomputation of worked examples, core theory values and Part C calculations (occupancy, depletion, Kd, kinetic and decay rates, competition, EC50, gain and messenger accumulation).

academic_self_review.method: Internal assessment only. Deductions: incomplete full-text source access, historical raw data not independently reanalyzed, no external exam calibration, no interactive device or full accessibility testing.

static_checks.adjacent_navigation: Both 3.D.12 and 4.A.02 already have reciprocal dynamic navigation to 4.A.01.

limitations: Internal reviews, not external peer review.
MP SET 2024 archived mirror; current primary MPPSC-hosted syllabus not independently verified.
Accessible bibliographic records and source material consulted; not every primary paper read in full.
Static source/coordinate/label checks only, not complete browser/device or accessibility audit.
Pages workflow and public HTTP availability separately verified after commit.
